q1.name: FP | Abdelhakim Boukeffoussa | Qualified Email 1
q1.subject: The first handoff that usually fails
q1.html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Most first hires don't fail because the person is bad. They fail because the task was handed off without the context.

That's why every task in your plan comes with a brief: the goal, the context, the constraints, what "done" looks like, and how much they can decide alone. Pareto calls it the Black Box method. You define what goes in and what comes out. What happens in the middle is their job.

If your plan showed 10+ hours a week, that's a full-time Right Hand's job. A 20-minute Matching Call turns your plan into a profile: Book a 20-minute Matching Call

The Pareto Talent team

n1.subject: How to brief a task in 2 minutes
n1.html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The plan gave you a brief for each task. Here's how to use them well:

  1. Fill the [brackets] with your real details. Specifics beat good intentions.
  2. Send one brief at a time, starting with Week 1.
  3. Agree on the "definition of done" before the work starts, not after.

Your plan, anytime: Open my 40-Hour Handoff Plan

n3.name: FP | Abdelhakim Boukeffoussa | Nurture Email 3
n3.subject: Check the work without micromanaging
n3.html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The fastest way to kill a handoff is to redo the work. The second fastest is to never check it.

The middle path: 10 minutes a day. Ask three things. What got done? What's blocked? What needs my decision?

When your plan grows past 10 hours a week, that's a full-time Right Hand's job. That's the moment to talk to Pareto: Book a 20-minute Matching Call

The Pareto Talent team
